  intro coefficient selector system fc dc fs ds fx dx permutation
  have undo (p : selector → system ≃ system) :

            (coefficient := coefficient) (fun s => (p s).symm)) *
        QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix
          (QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.controlledSystemEquiv p) = 1
    rw [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix_mul]
    have cancel :
        (QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.controlledSystemEquiv
          (coefficient := coefficient) p).trans
          (QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.controlledSystemEquiv
            (fun s => (p s).symm)) = Equiv.refl _ := by
      ext ⟨c, s, x⟩ <;>
        simp [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.controlledSystemEquiv]
    rw [cancel]
    ext row column
    simp [QuantumBlockEncoding.Robin.ComplexLCU.equivPermutationMatrix,
      Matrix.one_apply]
  exact ⟨undo permutation, by simpa using undo (fun s => (permutation s).symm)⟩
probes.natural_language_answer: On every basis state, F_q F_p(c,(s,x))=(c,(s,p_s⁻¹(p_s(x))))=(c,(s,x)); the reverse composite similarly uses p_s(p_s⁻¹(x))=x. Both composites read the preserved selector s. A matrix with column k equal to |F(k)⟩ composes as U_g U_f=U_{g∘f}; hence both matrix products equal I_A. This is a generic theorem, not inference from a few finite examples.

probes.natural_language_answer: Use C={*}, S={false,true}, X={0,1,2}. On selector false let p exchange 0 and 1 and let q exchange 1 and 2; on selector true let both be identity. From |*,false,0⟩, U_r gives |*,false,2⟩, while U_p U_q applies q first and gives |*,false,1⟩. At row |*,false,2⟩ and the given input column the two amplitudes are 1 and 0. Repair the product to U_q U_p, or change r_s to p_s∘q_s. A two-level system alone would miss this mechanism because its permutations commute.

          (coefficient := coefficient) second) *

probes.natural_language_answer: F_q(F_p(c,(s,x)))=(c,(s,q_s(p_s(x))))=F_r(c,(s,x)). In the matrix entry (U_q U_p)(a,b), the U_p factor is nonzero only at the intermediate basis label k=F_p(b); the surviving U_q entry is 1 exactly when a=F_q(F_p(b)). Thus the product is U_r, with p applied first on column vectors. No commutativity assumption is present.
